newsitem.title: BELGIUM: ACEA sees 1997 growth in W. Europe car sales.
newsitem.headline: ACEA sees 1997 growth in W. Europe car sales.

text.p: New passenger car registrations in Western Europe are expected to grow by about 1.8 percent in 1997, a spokesman for the European Automobile Manufacturers Association (ACEA) said on Thursday.
ACEA spokesman James Rosenstein said this was a "guarded estimate of probable growth" and that the figure could turn out to be lower. "Nobody expects strong growth," he told Reuters.

Earlier, ACEA said new passenger car registrations fell by 2.9 percent to 1,130,000 units in January compared with the same period last year, mainly due to plunging sales in France following the phasing out of a state incentive scheme last year.
In 1996, car registrations rose 6.6 percent in the 15-member European Union, Norway, Switzerland and Liechtenstein to 12,803,700.
